medicines.name: Metformin
medicines.plain_language_explanation: This medicine helps control your blood sugar by reducing the amount of glucose your liver releases. It is one of the first medicines prescribed for type 2 diabetes.
medicines.safety_note: Never stop this medicine on your own. If you feel unusually tired or breathless, contact your doctor immediately.

medicines.name: Amlodipine
medicines.plain_language_explanation: This medicine relaxes your blood vessels so your heart does not have to pump as hard, which helps lower blood pressure.
medicines.safety_note: Do not stop suddenly. Some people notice ankle swelling — tell your doctor if this happens.

medicines.name: Aspirin
medicines.timing: After breakfast — NEVER on empty stomach
medicines.plain_language_explanation: A low dose of aspirin helps prevent blood clots from forming in your arteries, which can reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke.
medicines.safety_note: Always take with food. Tell your doctor if you notice any black stools or stomach pain.

medicines.name: Vitamin D3
medicines.plain_language_explanation: Vitamin D3 is a supplement that helps your body absorb calcium and keeps your bones strong. Many Indians are deficient in Vitamin D due to limited sun exposure.
medicines.safety_note: This is a supplement, not a drug. Take exactly as prescribed — taking too much Vitamin D can be harmful.
